cards.explanation: The answer is False. David says, “His enemies are scattered, and those who hate Him flee His presence.” When God arises, the ones who hate Him are the ones running. I bet not one of them stops to look back.

The answer is that the righteous rejoice and celebrate with joy. David says, “But the righteous will be glad and rejoice before God; they will celebrate with joy.” The wicked will perish as wax melts before the fire, but the righteous are glad to be there before God. Same moment, two very different reactions, friends.

The answer is True. David calls God “…Him who rides on the clouds…” in verse 4, and then says, “A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in His holy habitation.” It's the same song and the same God. The One up in the clouds is the One who defends widows.

The answer is that God settles the lonely in families. David says, “God settles the lonely in families…” The lonely don't get left on their own. God puts them in a family. I think that's one of the warmest lines in the whole psalm.

The answer is shook. David says, “…the earth shook and the heavens poured down rain before God, the One on Sinai…” (Psalm 68:8). When God marched, the ground itself felt it. Even the earth had a reaction, friends.

The answer is that the rain refreshed it. David says, “You sent abundant rain, O God; You refreshed Your weary inheritance.” The inheritance was weary, and the rain refreshed it. It's like getting a cold glass of water after a long day on your feet.

The answer is the poor. David says, “O God, from Your bounty You provided for the poor.” The bounty is God's, and the poor are who He provides for. Earlier David calls Him “A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows…” (Psalm 68:5), so this fits, friends.

The answer is that they flee in haste. The women's song says, “Kings and their armies flee in haste…” (Psalm 68:12). It's a whole army, and they aren't marching anywhere but away. Haste means they're in a big hurry.

The answer is she who waits at home. The song says, “she who waits at home divides the plunder.” The one who stayed home is the one dividing it up. It's like the one who stayed home watching the oven and still gets to hand out the cookies.

The answer is the mountain God chose to dwell on. David asks, “Why do you gaze in envy, O mountains of many peaks?” and answers, “This is the mountain God chose for His dwelling…” Those big mountains with all their peaks are looking at the one God chose. I think that's a lot of mountain jealousy, friends.
The answer is True. David says of the chosen mountain, “…where the LORD will surely dwell forever.” Surely and forever, both in one line. That's about as settled as it gets, friends.
The answer is False. David doesn't say hundreds. He says the chariots of God are tens of thousands, thousands of thousands. That's way past what I could count, even with a helper.

The answer is so the LORD God may dwell there. David says God received gifts, even from the rebellious, “…that the LORD God may dwell there.” The ascending, the captives and the gifts all lead to God dwelling there. David gives that as the reason, friends.

The answer is even from death. David says, “Our God is a God of deliverance; the Lord GOD is our rescuer from death.” Not just from trouble. From death itself. That's about as far as rescue can reach, friends.

The answer is False. I think this verse is heavy. David says, “Surely God will crush the heads of His enemies, the hairy crowns of those who persist in guilty ways.” He doesn't say God makes peace with them.

The answer is the singers. David says, “The singers lead the way, the musicians follow after, among the maidens playing tambourines.” The singers are out in front and the musicians come right behind them. Not a quiet group, I'd say.

The answer is True. David says, “Bless God in the great congregation; bless the LORD from the fountain of Israel.” He's calling for a big crowd to bless God together. It's a call for everybody, not for a quiet corner, friends.

The answer is gifts. David says, “Because of Your temple at Jerusalem kings will bring You gifts.” Kings are coming, and they come carrying gifts for God. It's a good thing to show up with something in your hands, friends.

The answer is the nations who delight in war. David prays, “Scatter the nations who delight in war.” He names them by what they enjoy, and it's war. Those are the ones he asks God to scatter, friends.

The answer is that Cush stretches out her hands to God. David says, “Envoys will arrive from Egypt; Cush will stretch out her hands to God.” Envoys arrive from Egypt. And Cush, a land south of Egypt, stretches out her hands to God.

The answer is False. David says, “Ascribe the power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, whose strength is in the skies.” His majesty is over Israel, and His strength is in the skies. That's where the verse puts it, not down on the ground, friends.
